agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-01 step 3 of 5
summary_for_principal: Step 3 of 5: the validator that checks everything the schema alone can't — rules V3 through V15. Every rule is its own function; each one has at least one example that should pass and one that should be refused, including every 'looks fine but isn't' case the work package specifically asked for (a route that looks like it covers every case but misses one; a gate that lets a refusal slip through unrouted; a reviewer that could approve its own work; and others). Building this surfaced two real mistakes in step 1's work: two checks (a gate's kind, an ending's message) had accidentally been enforced too early, in the wrong layer, which would have made two of this step's own required test cases impossible to write. Both are technical layering corrections, fixed directly. 45 new tests, all passing on Python 3.10-3.12. A full run against the spec's own worked example (Appendix A) correctly reports only the expected 'not registered' notices (nothing in this repository yet supplies the real building blocks it calls) and nothing else — no false alarms.

filled_in.gap: V4 ('a type mismatch in in, out or collect') doesn't say how permissively types should be compared — e.g. whether an integer value may satisfy a `number`-typed input, or whether a narrower enum may satisfy a broader one.
filled_in.assumed: A pragmatic compatibility rule: `any` matches everything; an integer satisfies a declared `number`; a list/map is compatible if its item type is; an enum satisfies a declared enum if its members are a subset; everything else must match exactly. Reversible and local to one helper function (_types_compatible).
filled_in.reversal_cost: Cheap — one function, no fixture depends on an edge case this rule doesn't already cover correctly.

filled_in.gap: V15 ('a closed value set with no grounded_in') doesn't say which documents introduce a 'closed value set' — only Profile and Control carry a grounded_in field at all, and Control's own type/severity vocabulary is the *format's* closed set (already grounded by the spec itself), not something each Control document introduces.
filled_in.assumed: Scoped V15 to Profile documents whose own embedded JSON Schema declares at least one `enum` — the clearest, most literal reading of 'a closed value set' as something a document's author is introducing, not the format's own fixed vocabulary. Did not extend it to Control, Tool or Process documents.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Cheap to widen later — additive, one more check function.

filled_in.gap: V10's 'self-reachable' isn't defined precisely — direct self-recursion only, or reachable through a chain of other Processes?
filled_in.assumed: Full chain: built a call graph across every Process the registry holds (via each Tool of mechanism kind PROCESS) and checked reachability back to the process under validation, not just a direct self-call. The more literal reading of 'can reach itself', and the fail-closed one — a narrower direct-only check would miss real indirect recursion.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Cheap — the narrower check is a subset of the graph walk already written.

options_rejected: Write the V9/V14 fixtures against a document that fails for a different reason and call it close enough: rejected — the resulting finding would carry the wrong rule id, which defeats the point of a rule-labelled fixture.
decisions.cost_to_change: Two JSON Schema fields, already done; no existing fixture depended on the stricter version (checked: none did).

untouched.divergence: V11's 'two branches writing one REPLACE channel' check walks forward from each PARALLEL branch collecting state writes until it reaches the JOIN node, following STEP/ROUTE edges only — it does not follow into a nested PARALLEL, GATE, or FOR_EACH inside a branch to collect writes from further inside those constructs.
untouched.why_not_now: No fixture in this repository (or the spec's own examples) nests a PARALLEL/GATE/FOR_EACH inside a parallel branch; extending the walk to recurse into every node type correctly is real additional work with no fixture yet to prove it against, and WP-01's acceptance criteria don't name this specific nesting case.

lessons.maxim: Before adding a JSON Schema constraint, check the spec's own §14 rule table for which rule number governs it — the boundary between 'the schema refuses this' (V1) and 'the validator refuses this' (V3-V15) is a decision made once, in the table, not something to re-derive per field by asking 'could the schema catch this cheaply'.
lessons.incident: Step 1 added `enum: [APPROVAL, INPUT]` to GATE.kind and `minLength: 1` to ending.says, both of which spec §14 explicitly assigns to V9 and V14 respectively — found only when this step tried to write the exact fixtures WP-01 A3 asks for and discovered the schema had already made them unwritable.
lessons.destination: any future WP-01-style PR that adds a JSON Schema field for this format
